column1: # Single GEMM / convolution, strict f32, batch 1. Meganeura runs 3 processes per shape and keeps the median gpu_ms row; PyTorch runs once.
# RTX 5070 (driver 595, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130) and Arc B570 (Mesa 26.0.3 ANV, PyTorch 2.13.0+xpu), i5-12400F, November 8, 2026,
#   Meganeura 6b1e784 (main 134e990 plus this branch) with examples/op_bench.rs as committed with this file.
# RX 7900 XT (gfx1100, RADV Mesa 26.0.8, PyTorch 2.13.0+rocm7.2, Ryzen 5 9600X), November 8, 2026, Meganeura 429a0e4.
# Meganeura: MEGANEURA_TUNE=1 (2 s kernel tuner, 64 MiB scratch; the 4096 GEMM exceeds it) MEGANEURA_DISABLE_COOP=1, e-graph optimizer off.
#   gpu_ms = one timestamped pass over 30 copies of the operation on the same input and weight, a barrier after every dispatch, / 30;
#   median of 30 steps. Shape-preserving convolutions (all 3x3 rows) are chained, each copy reading the previous output; their
#   Winograd weight transforms still run first, which leaves the 512-channel row's transformed weights out of cache.
# PyTorch: TF32 off, cudnn.benchmark on, profiler off during timing (profiling perturbs ROCm execution).
#   gpu_ms = device events around one replay of a graph of 30 serial ops / 30, median of 30 replays (includes device dispatch gaps,
#   excludes host enqueue gaps). Graph outputs match eager within 1e-6 relative (bitwise except last-bit XPU differences).
# wall_ms is not comparable across engines: Meganeura's is a step of 30 copies / 30 with MEGANEURA_GPU_TIMING=1; PyTorch's is one eager call.
# tflops = GEMM or direct-convolution FLOPs / gpu_ms (effective for Winograd). Kernel labels: MatMul[MxNxK]. Inputs differ between engines.
# gemm dims: M K N; conv dims: Cin H W Cout k stride pad (data/op-bench/shapes.txt).
# Dispatch floor (eltwise rows), RTX 5070 and Arc B570 as above, November 8, 2026, Meganeura 031f7b5 with this file's op_bench.
#   A 256-element f32 add. add-256: 30 chained adds, each reading the previous sum (a barrier after each dispatch);
#   add-256-indep: 30 adds of the same input, one barrier group. PyTorch's stream runs both in order.
#   add-256-single: one add per step, run without MEGANEURA_GPU_TIMING (gpu_ms NaN); wall_ms is one step() + wait() round trip,
#   against one eager PyTorch add + synchronize. In the other two rows wall_ms is a step of 30 adds / 30 (Meganeura, timed)
